mn61:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary.
mn61:2.1: Now on that occasion the venerable Rāhula[^1] was living at Ambalatthika.
mn61:2.2: Then when it was evening the Blessed One rose from meditation, and went to the venerable Rāhula at Ambalatthika.
mn61:2.3: The venerable Rāhula saw the Blessed One coming from afar.
mn61:2.4: When he saw him, he made a seat ready and set out water for washing the feet.
mn61:2.5: The Blessed One sat down on the seat made ready.
mn61:2.6: Having sat down, he washed his feet.
mn61:2.7: The venerable Rāhula paid homage to him and sat down at one side.
mn61:3.1: Then the Blessed One poured the little remaining quantity of water into the water-dipper, and he addressed the venerable Rāhula thus:
mn61:3.2: ‘Rāhula, do you see this little remaining quantity of water poured into the water-dipper?’
mn61:3.4: ‘Unless people are careful not to speak falsehood knowingly, there is as little of the monk in them as this.’
mn61:4.1: Then the Blessed One threw away the little remaining water, and he addressed the venerable Rāhula thus:
mn61:4.2: ‘Rāhula, do you see that little remaining water thrown away?’
mn61:4.4: ‘Unless people are careful not to speak falsehood knowingly, what there is of the monk in them is thrown away like that.’
mn61:5.1: Then the Blessed One turned the water-dipper upside down, and he addressed the venerable Rāhula thus:
mn61:5.2: ‘Rāhula, do you see this water-dipper turned upside down?’
mn61:5.4: ‘Unless people are careful not to speak falsehood knowingly, what there is of the monk in them is turned upside down like that.’
mn61:6.1: Then the Blessed One turned the water-dipper right way up again, and he addressed the venerable Rāhula thus:
mn61:6.2: ‘Rāhula, do you see this hollow, empty water-dipper?’
mn61:6.4: ‘Unless people are careful not to speak falsehood knowingly, what there is of the monk in them is as hollow and empty as that.
mn61:7.1: ‘Suppose, Rāhula, there were a royal tusker elephant with tusks as long as chariot poles, full-grown in stature, highly bred, and well used to battles, and in a battle he used his fore feet and his hind feet and his fore quarters and his hind quarters and his head and his ears and his tusks and his tail, and yet he kept his trunk back;
mn61:7.2: then it would occur to his mahout:
mn61:7.3: “This royal tusker elephant with tusks as long as chariot poles, full-grown in stature, highly bred, and well used to battles, in a battle uses his fore feet and his hind feet … and his tail, and yet he keeps his trunk back.
mn61:7.4: The royal tusker elephant has not yet given up his life to the king.”
mn61:7.5: But as soon as the royal tusker elephant, in a battle, uses his fore feet and his hind feet … and his tail, and his trunk as well, then it would occur to his mahout:
mn61:7.6: “This royal tusker elephant with tusks as long as chariot poles, full-grown in stature, highly bred, and well used to battles, in a battle uses his fore feet and his hind feet and his fore quarters and his hind quarters and his head and his ears and his tusks and his tail, and his trunk as well.
mn61:7.7: The royal tusker elephant has given up his life to the king.
mn61:7.8: There is nothing more now that the royal tusker elephant will not do.”
mn61:7.9: So too, Rāhula, as long as anyone is not ashamed of speaking a deliberate lie, I say there is no evil he will not do.
mn61:7.10: Therefore, Rāhula, you should train thus: “I shall not utter a falsehood even in jest” —
mn61:7.11: that is how you should train, Rāhula.’
mn61:8.2: what is the purpose of a looking-glass?’
mn61:8.3: ‘For the purpose of reflection, venerable sir.’
mn61:8.4: ‘So too, Rāhula, bodily kamma should be done with continual reflection, verbal kamma should be done with continual reflection, mental kamma should be done with continual reflection.
mn61:9.1: ‘Rāhula, whatever kamma you desire to do by the body, that same bodily kamma of yours should be reviewed thus:
mn61:9.2: “Would this kamma that I desire to do by the body lead to the affliction of myself, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both—
mn61:9.3: is it unprofitable bodily kamma with painful consequences, with painful results?”
mn61:9.4: If, when you review it, you know thus:
mn61:9.5: “This kamma that I desire to do by the body would lead to the affliction of myself, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both—
mn61:9.6: it is unprofitable bodily kamma with painful consequences, with painful results”, then such kamma of body is definitely not to be done by you.
mn61:9.7: But if, when you review it, you know thus:
mn61:9.8: “This kamma that I desire to do by the body would not lead to the affliction of myself, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both—
mn61:9.9: it is profitable bodily kamma with pleasant consequences, with pleasant results”, then such kamma of body may be done by you.
mn61:10.1: ‘While you are doing a kamma by the body, that same bodily kamma of yours should be reviewed thus:
mn61:10.2: “Does this kamma that I am doing by the body lead to the affliction of myself, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both—
mn61:10.3: is it unprofitable bodily kamma with painful consequences, with painful results?”
mn61:10.4: If, when you review it, you know thus:
mn61:10.5: “This kamma that I am doing by the body leads to the affliction of myself, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both—
mn61:10.6: it is unprofitable bodily kamma with painful consequences, with painful results”, you should suspend such bodily kamma.
mn61:10.7: But if, when you review it, you know thus:
mn61:10.8: “This kamma that I am doing by the body does not lead to the affliction of myself, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both—
mn61:10.9: it is profitable bodily kamma with pleasant consequences, with pleasant results”, you may continue with such bodily kamma.
mn61:11.1: ‘Having done a kamma by the body, that same bodily kamma of yours should be reviewed thus:
mn61:11.2: “Did this kamma that I did by the body lead to the affliction of myself, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both—

mn61:11.5: “This kamma that I did by the body led to the affliction of myself, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both—

mn61:18.1: ‘Whatever monks or divines there have been in the past who purified their bodily kamma, their verbal kamma and their mental kamma, all of them did so by repeatedly reviewing in just this way.
mn61:18.2: Whatever monks or divines there will be in the future who will purify their bodily kamma, their verbal kamma and their mental kamma, all of them will do so by repeatedly reviewing in just this way.
mn61:18.3: Whatever monks or divines there are now who are purifying their bodily kamma, their verbal kamma and their mental kamma, all of them do so by repeatedly reviewing in just this way.
mn61:18.4: Therefore, Rāhula, you should train thus: “We shall purify our bodily kamma, our verbal kamma and our mental kamma by repeatedly reviewing them”—
mn61:18.5: that is how you should train, Rāhula.’
mn61:18.6: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn61:18.7: The venerable Rāhula was satisfied, and he delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
